title.narrative: Provision of targeted emergency food assistance (TEFA) to vulnerable food insecure populations in North Yemen

description.narrative: This project aims to support the provision, procurement and distribution of wheat flour to food insecure populations in North Yemen through the Targeted Emergency Food Assistance (TEFA) activity. Yemen remains among the world's most food insecure countries with 64% of households unable to access food (inadequate food consumption levels). Specifically in the North, 65% of households reported inadequate food consumption levels. As of August, this was the fourth consecutive month of a steady increase in food insecurity. In the North, WFP has implemented a pause in its General Food Distribution activities to agree with authorities on a way forward on a retargeting and registration pilot, while WFP was able to successfully carry out a retargeting pilot, the funding constraints increased, leading WFP to pivot its programming. The previous General Food Assistance activity will not resume and will be replaced by a Targeted Emergency Food Assistance (TEFA) project. The key drivers of Yemen’s food crisis include the ongoing economic decline caused by conflict, which has led to inflation, currency devaluation, and the collapse of basic services. Compounding this, the pause in humanitarian food assistance since December 2023 has left many vulnerable households without support. Before the pause, half of the population in these areas relied on food distributions, and the suspension of aid has pushed many into extreme coping strategies. Additionally, climate shocks, such as flooding, have heightened food insecurity, particularly in agriculture-dependent households that are highly vulnerable to such disruptions.In response to these hardships, families in northern Yemen are adopting increasingly desperate measures. More than 50 percent of households are resorting to harmful coping strategies, including reducing food portions, skipping meals, borrowing food or money, and sacrificing adult meals so children can eat. Some families are even forced to sell off valuable assets or risk their lives by sending young men to the frontlines to earn an income.The food security crisis in northern Yemen has reached critical levels, with millions of people at risk. Immediate and sustained humanitarian assistance is essential to prevent further deterioration and alleviate the severe suffering caused by widespread hunger and malnutrition.The new Targeted Emergency Food Assistance (TEFA) activity aims to reach up to 6 million affected people (as opposed to the 9.5 million prior to the pause). This significant reduction would be based on a geographically focused approach aimed at ensuring that aid reaches the most vulnerable while WFP continues the targeting and registration process in prioritized areas for assistance. With current funding, WFP can only provide food assistance for 2.6 million people in the most affected districts. The goal is to gradually increase and expand to 6 million people as resources allow.WFP will procure 4825.4 MT of wheat flour and reach 675,558 affected people with this allocation. The targeted governorates and districts are the following:Al Bayda: Ash Sharyah, Nati, Radman, Numan, As SawadiyahAl Hodeidah: Al Qanawis, Jabal Ras, Bura, Al HujjaylahAmran: Dhulaymat Habur, Al Ashah, Maswar, Qaflat Odhar, Suwayr, As SudahHajjah: Khayran Al Muharraq, Bani Qays, Washhah, Bakil Al Mir, Aflah Ash Sham, Qarah, Al Maghrabah, Aflah Al YamanRaymah: Bilad Attaam, As SalafiyyahAt the operationalization strategy, WFP was planning on using the CERF allocation for the procurement of 3 separate commodities. However, after careful review of the pipeline, the decision was made to focus on the procurement of wheat flour solely to ensure that all gaps are covered. To this end, the planned number of targeted people has been reviewed to reflect the new level of reach, which is slightly over twice the estimate. This will allow WFP to reach more affected people, maximize the impact and effectively manage available funds and delivery of assistance.
